top_story: Trump’s March threat to destroy Iran’s power grid unless Tehran reopens the Strait of Hormuz set a wider coercive frame that Tehran answered with warnings of regional escalation, raising the risk that local fronts would absorb the pressure. That backdrop has sharpened in recent days as Israeli strikes in Lebanon killed 18 and wounded 124 over one day, including six killed in southern Lebanon just hours after a ceasefire extension, exposing how fragile de-escalation has become. In Gaza, the absence of allowed recovery equipment has left Palestinians digging through rubble by hand for relatives, showing how military pressure and siege conditions are compounding civilian trauma long after strikes hit. The regional picture is one of expanding coercion with weak restraints, where threats at the state level are feeding violence that civilians are forced to absorb across multiple fronts.
